summary: The Relief Without Delay Act requires the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to continue all disaster relief, recovery, and mitigation operations using the Disaster Relief Fund during a lapse in federal appropriations. It exempts FEMA operations from government shutdown restrictions under the Anti-Deficiency Act, requires regular reporting on disaster relief fund obligations and disbursements, requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to assess housing and infrastructure unmet needs following major disasters, directs NOAA and FEMA to establish a program to improve tornado detection and warning capabilities, and creates a grant program for community tornado resilience in high-risk areas.

affected_groups.effect: Must continue operations during funding lapses, maintain personnel and contract support, follow new reporting requirements, and coordinate tornado programs with NOAA.

Receive uninterrupted disaster relief, recovery, and mitigation funding and claims processing during government shutdowns, alongside access to new tornado resilience grants and community shelter funding.
affected_groups.group: Disaster victims and state, local, tribal, and territorial governments

affected_groups.effect: Required to evaluate disaster housing and infrastructure damage and report on unmet needs following major disaster declarations.
affected_groups.group: Department of Housing and Urban Development

affected_groups.effect: Required to collaborate with FEMA on a national tornado detection and warning improvement plan and interagency coordination.

key_provisions: FEMA must continue all disaster relief, recovery, and mitigation operations funded through the Disaster Relief Fund during a lapse in appropriations.
Unobligated balances in the Disaster Relief Fund remain available for expenditure during a lapse in appropriations, and funds may not be withheld or reprogrammed except under the Anti-Deficiency Act.
FEMA operations authorized by the Act are classified as essential and exempt from government shutdown restrictions.
FEMA must submit monthly reports to Congress detailing Disaster Relief Fund obligations, disbursements, and project statuses, and publish them online.
The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development must evaluate damage and identify housing and infrastructure unmet needs within 60 days of a major disaster declaration and quarterly thereafter.
NOAA and FEMA must establish a program to improve tornado detection, forecasting, and warning capabilities using technologies like advanced radar and artificial intelligence.

FEMA must establish a grant program for state and local emergency management agencies to support tornado preparedness, constructing community storm shelters, and modernizing warning systems, prioritizing high-risk and low-income communities.

summary_detail.plain_summary: The Relief Without Delay Act requires the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to continue all disaster relief, recovery, and mitigation operations using the Disaster Relief Fund during a lapse in federal appropriations. It exempts FEMA operations from government shutdown restrictions under the Anti-Deficiency Act, requires regular reporting on disaster relief fund obligations and disbursements, requires the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to assess housing and infrastructure unmet needs following major disasters, directs NOAA and FEMA to establish a program to improve tornado detection and warning capabilities, and creates a grant program for community tornado resilience in high-risk areas.
summary_detail.significance: This bill ensures that federal disaster relief funding and operations continue uninterrupted during government shutdowns by exempting FEMA from standard funding lapse restrictions and utilizing existing disaster funds. It also introduces mandatory reporting for disaster spending, post-disaster unmet needs assessments by HUD, and targeted federal investments in tornado detection, forecasting, and community resilience grants.
